newsitem.title: GERMANY: Man dies, 53 injured in German asylum home blaze.
newsitem.headline: Man dies, 53 injured in German asylum home blaze.

text.p: One man died and 53 people, including nine children, were injured on Wednesday in a fire in an asylum seekers' hostel in the southern German town of Friedrichshafen, police said.
They said they were not yet sure what had caused the blaze, but that an arson attack could not be ruled out.
Germany is particularly sensitive to fires in foreigners' homes and asylum-seekers' hostels since a number of them were targeted in a wave of racist violence after unification in 1990.
When the fire broke out in the early hours of the morning, 320 people were asleep in the two-storey former military barracks. Many of them climbed to safety down knotted bed-sheets.
The dead man, a 26-year-old Kurdish Turk, was found in a first floor room. Five people broke bones jumping from the building and others inhaled smoke from the blaze.
Police said there had been a bomb threat against the hostel in the past, but they had found no connection between this and the blaze, which did most damage around the entrance to the building.
They said fire protection doors were not properly closed, and some had been propped open, allowing smoke to spread through the building.
Just over a week ago, suspected right-wing extremists set fire to a church in the north German town of Luebeck, prompting politicians and religious leaders to call for a clampdown on extremists.
The attackers daubed Nazi swastikas on the walls and scrawled the name of a local priest whose parish is sheltering a family of asylum seekers to prevent their deportation to Algeria.
